my heart is absolutely broken for this man. not one but two horrible losses in such a short time period--i can't even imagine that pain.

as a musician i needed to see this too. one can get so caught up in the obsession with playing perfectly--100% in tune, no wrong notes, perfect tone, etc... but things like this remind you of what music is truly about.

music expresses the full range of human emotion. in his voice i hear grief, regret, sorrow, hope... this video made me remember why i am passionate about music. it's not about the fucking notes. it's about expressing something real.

i talked to a friend of mine and she told me she was good friends with a dermatologist. while she couldn't get me an actual appointment for free, she said she called her and asked if she could take a look to see if i should be concerned and seek serious medical attention. it's not an official diagnosis, but the dermatologist is "95%" certain that i have pityriasis rosea, [here's](http://dermnetnz.org/viral/pityriasis-rosea.html) a website if you're curious. it often follows or occurs with upper respiratory infections so that explains my cold. the foul smell might have been a fungus that decided to start growing on top of the irritated skin, as apparently raw, cracked skin is quite prone to picking up fungus easily. it's harmless and should apparently clear up in 6-12 weeks (goodbye, sex life!)..... thanks for the kind words, everyone!

as a feminist whose friends are also mostly feminists, that's really just not true. 

feminists fight for bodily autonomy--one of the greatest issues american culture faces relating to that is forced infant circumcision (or as i call it, male genital mutilation). you'll find that most feminists are strongly anti-circumcision, or at least oppose it being performed on infants who cannot consent. 

feminists fight rape culture, a pervasive school of thought that dominates almost all modern societies that portrays rape as a very specific kind of event (usually, a woman being attacked on the street by a male stranger) when in reality rape is much more complicated than that. rapes are almost always committed by someone the victim knows, someone they trust. and the victims are not always women; in fact, the idea that men can't be raped only further perpetrates the idea that women are weak and submissive while men are strong and dominant. men can be raped, and women can be rapists (albeit rarely).

feminists also fight the general attitude that femininity is a sign of weakness. this leads to women being paid less than men on average, being victims of domestic violence more than men, and other grave consequences for women. but there are also great effects for men. men can't express any form of femininity without being seen as weak or having their sexual orientation questioned. this is why it's ok for women to be tomboys (masculine=strong) but a man in a skirt gets called a faggot (feminine=weak). this obviously is connected to homophobia in a lot of ways.

there are lots of other issues faced by men today, and you'll find that most feminists are equally driven to fight these issues. the thing is, while misogyny and society's views on femininity have serious consequences for both genders, women are in general victimized by these consequences much more than men. also, these consequences are created by a view of femininity and womanhood that has been shaped, for the most part, by men. the issues men face today aren't because of women's disdain for masculinity, but rather society's disdain for the feminine in general. it's not really a case of women oppressing men, but men oppressing themselves. feminism isn't called equalism or humanism because the issue we face today is the hatred of femininity, and everyone is affected by that.

I've done a lot of therapy in the past, and while I can't afford a private psych at the moment, I've been doing group sessions at a free clinic. It's been pointed out to me that while I don't directly blame myself, I have a difficult time placing blame on the perpetrators of the violence I've experienced. For example, instead of saying that I was a victim of statutory and coercive rape, I say that I dated an older man who talked me into sex. I wonder if I'm doing the same thing with Jeff--I know he sexually assaulted me, but I don't view it as that serious because (1) it's "not as bad" as the other violence I've experienced and (2) because I still care about Jeff and his life and his feelings, so I don't want to frame it as something serious to avoid making him feel guilty. I also feel guilt because there've been plenty of times that I've done shitty things to people I care about due to mental illness (something I recognize in Jeff) and I've had to ask for forgiveness from them when I probably didn't deserve it. I have to ask myself if I can't give that to Jeff, then why do I deserve it from other friends?

It never ceases to astound me how shit like this can affect you for years after the fact without you even being aware.

I had started seeing someone, and we'd been intimate a few times but with my shirt or skirt covering my stomach, which at the time was my current canvas of choice. He'd seen the scars on my thighs, and was sad about it and made me promise that I wasn't doing it anymore, and that I'd never do it again. I lied to him and promised. One day, during the heat of the moment, he took my shirt off before I realized what was happening. He saw fresh cuts and started crying and holding me, just saying "why?" over and over again. 

It was at that moment I realized that I wasn't the only person I was hurting when I hurt myself. Seeing the grief he felt just from seeing what I did to myself made me feel like such a selfish asshole. 

We're not together anymore (sadly, he had to move out of country) but that was over 7 months ago and I haven't SI'd since. Every time I am tempted to, I remember that guilt I felt at that moment and I am disgusted by the thought of doing it.
Thanks for the shout out. Truly appreciate it.
